animations.title: Lambda execution lifecycle
objectives: Place Init before the first handler Invoke.
Explain why a later invocation may reuse an idle environment.
Explain why overlapping invokes need another environment for a standard Event Function.
Connect environment growth to downstream database connection pressure.
Explain eventual Shutdown and why process state is not durable.
assumptions: Standard on-demand Lambda Event Function with synchronous direct invocation; this is not Lambda Managed Instances or Lambda Web Functions.
Lambda has no ready environment for request 1, retains A for request 2, and has capacity to create B for request 3. These are illustrated outcomes, not guarantees.
Horizontal distances and video duration are conceptual. They do not assert AWS latency or scaling times.
Each active environment may open one database connection in this example; actual application behavior may differ.
The database lane illustrates connection demand, not the timing of SQL calls or database execution.
animations.hinglish: Request 1 ke liye A ka Init hota hai, phir handler Invoke. A idle bache to request 2 use reuse kar sakti hai. Jab A busy ho aur request 3 aaye, standard Event Function ko B jaisa alag environment chahiye. B apna Init karta hai. Do active invokes ka matlab do database connection demands bhi ho sakte hain; DB limit separate measure karo.

sources.supports: one active invoke per standard Event Function environment, concurrency and controls

cues.text: First request arrives. In this example, Lambda has no ready environment.
Lambda creates environment A. Runtime and code outside the handler initialize before Invoke.
After Init, the handler processes request one. Init adds latency to this cold invocation.
A later request can reuse idle environment A. Static initialization does not repeat on this warm path.
Request two reuses A in this example. Handler runs without another Init phase.
Request three overlaps request two. A is busy, so Lambda needs another environment for this on-demand Event Function.
Lambda creates environment B. B has its own Init phase, then handles request three.
If each environment opens a database connection, more environments can increase connection demand.
Defend a limit: bound concurrency, pool connections where suitable, and measure throttles and database saturation.
Lambda eventually shuts environments down. Do not store durable application state only in process memory or temporary files.

checkpoints.prompt: Before request 1 runs its handler, what must finish?
checkpoints.feedback: Sahi. New environment pehle runtime aur static code initialize karta hai; phir handler Invoke hota hai.

checkpoints.prompt: If request 2 reuses idle A, does normal static Init run again?
options: No, A can invoke without repeating Init
Only if the database is full
checkpoints.feedback: Sahi. Warm reuse par normal Init repeat nahi hoti. Reuse itself guaranteed nahi hai.

checkpoints.prompt: A is still processing request 2. Where can request 3 run?
options: Inside A at the same time
In another environment B, if capacity permits
checkpoints.feedback: Sahi. Standard Event Function mein ek environment ek active invoke handle karta hai. B ko apna Init chahiye.

checkpoints.prompt: Two environments can each open a DB connection. If all DB slots are used, what should you examine first?
options: Bound demand and measure DB saturation
Assume a warm start solves connections
checkpoints.feedback: Sahi. Compute scaling DB capacity nahi banati. Cap, pooling, query load aur caller throttles measure karo.
